question: Which transport corridor improves India’s connectivity to Central Asia via Chabahar Port?
solution:
The correct answer is __**International North–South Transport Corridor (INSTC)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The International North–South Transport Corridor (INSTC)** is a **multi-modal transport network** established to enhance connectivity between **India, Central Asia, Russia, and Europe**. It aims to provide a faster, cost-effective trade route. ***Hence, this is the correct option.***
 
• The corridor passes through **India, Iran, and Russia** and leverages the **Chabahar Port** in Iran to connect with Central Asian countries like **Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, and Turkmenistan**.
 
• The INSTC is a strategic initiative to enhance India's presence in **Eurasian markets**, bypassing traditional trade routes through the Suez Canal, which are longer and more time-consuming.
 
• The **Chabahar Port** is a critical component of this corridor as it provides India a direct gateway to Afghanistan and Central Asia, bypassing Pakistan.
 
• The transport corridor integrates **road, rail, and sea routes** to facilitate seamless trade. It is expected to reduce the transportation cost by **30%** and transit time by **40%** compared to traditional routes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **East–West Corridor:**

 
 
• The East–West Corridor is part of India’s **Golden Quadrilateral project**. It connects **Silchar in Assam to Porbandar in Gujarat**.
 
• It primarily focuses on improving domestic road connectivity rather than international trade routes.
 
• This corridor does not enhance India's connectivity to Central Asia. ***Hence, this option is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **India–Myanmar Highway:**
 
 
• The India–Myanmar Highway, also known as the **Trilateral Highway**, connects **India, Myanmar, and Thailand**.
 
• It is focused on improving India's connectivity to Southeast Asia, not Central Asia.
 
• This highway is part of India’s **Act East Policy**, promoting trade and cultural ties with Southeast Asian nations. ***Hence, this option is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **South Asian Maritime Route:**
 
 
• This route focuses on enhancing maritime connectivity within **South Asia**, involving countries like **India, Sri Lanka, Maldives, and Bangladesh**.
 
• It does not play a role in improving connectivity to Central Asia. ***Hence, this option is incorrect.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Features of INSTC:**

 
 
• The INSTC was established in **2000** through an agreement between **India, Russia, and Iran**.
 
• It spans a length of **7,200 km** and includes road, rail, and maritime transport systems.
 
• The corridor is expected to boost trade between **India and Eurasia**, especially in sectors like **textiles, pharmaceuticals, and agricultural products**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Chabahar Port:**
 
 
• The Chabahar Port, located in **southeastern Iran**, is India's first overseas port investment.
 
• It provides India an alternative to access Afghanistan and Central Asia, bypassing Pakistan.
 
• The port is strategically important for India’s **connectivity, trade, and energy security**.
 
 
 
• **Geopolitical Importance:**
 
 
• The INSTC enhances India's connectivity to **energy-rich Central Asia**, strengthening its geopolitical and economic influence.
 
• It counters China's influence in the region, especially through initiatives like the **Belt and Road Initiative (BRI)**.
